verses.1: There was also Lazarus from Bethany, from the town of Mary. And Martha, her sister.
verses.2: And Maryam was the one who rubbed the master with oil and also scraped his feet with her fingers. This happened because her brother Lazarus became sick.
verses.3: So, his sisters sent word to him, saying, “Lord, look at whom you are loving—he is weak.”
verses.4: And when Jesus heard this, he said, “This sickness is not fatal; it is rather a means for God’s glory. Through this sickness, the Son of God will be glorified.”
verses.5: Jesus loved Martha, his sister, and Lazarus as well.
verses.6: So when he heard that he was weak, he stayed there for two days.
verses.7: After that, he said to his disciples, “Let us go back to Judea again.”
verses.8: The disciples say to him, “Rabbi, now the Jews want to put you to death. Will you go there again?”
verses.9: Jesus replied, “Is it twelve hours in a day? If anyone walks around during the day, they won’t realize that they’re seeing the light of this world.”
verses.10: If someone walks in the night, he notices that there is no light around him.
verses.11: He said these things, and then he continued to say to them: “Lazarus, our friend, is in distress. But I will go and comfort him.”
verses.12: So said his disciples: “Lord, if he is to be saved, then let him be saved.”
verses.13: But Jesus accepted his death. They thought that he was talking about the time of sleep.
verses.14: Then Jesus said to them, “Lazarus has died.”
verses.15: And I rejoice in you, so that you may believe that I am not there. Instead, we go towards him.
verses.16: So said Thomas, also known as Didymus, to his classmates: “Let us go with them, so that we can die along with them.”
verses.17: When Jesus arrived, he found that the tomb already had four days’ worth of leaves covering it.
verses.18: And Bethany was located far away from Jerusalem, at a distance of fifteen stadia.
verses.19: Many of the Jews also went to Martha and Mary, asking them to help them in dealing with their brother.
verses.20: When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she rushed to meet him. Mary, however, remained seated in the house.
verses.21: Then Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if it were not for my brother, he would not have died.”
verses.22: And now I know that whatever the god asks of you, he will give to you.
verses.23: Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise up.”
verses.24: Mary says to him, “I know that he will rise again on the last day.”
verses.25: Jesus said to her, “I am the Resurrection and the Life. Whoever believes in me will live even after he dies.”
verses.26: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will not die forever. Do you believe this?
verses.27: He said to him, “Nai, Lord, I believe that you are indeed the Christ, the Son of God who came into the world.
verses.28: And after saying this, she left. Then Maryam, her sister, cried out in grief. The teacher took her hand and comforted her.
verses.29: And when she heard this, she rushed over to him quickly.
verses.30: But Jesus did not go into the town. He remained in the same place where Martha had taken him.
verses.31: So, those Jews who were with her in the house and who believed in her, seeing that Marya stood up quickly and left, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to pray there.
verses.32: So, when Mary saw where Jesus was, she fell at His feet and said to Him, “Lord, if only my brother hadn’t died.”
verses.33: Then Jesus, seeing her crying, and also the Jews who were with her crying, was filled with emotion in his spirit. He became agitated himself.
verses.34: And he said, “Where were you when he was killed?” They replied, “Lord, come and see for yourself.”
verses.36: So said the Jews. Look at how he treated him.
verses.37: But what did they say? This man, who had opened the eyes of the blind person, couldn’t possibly do this in order to prevent that person from dying.
verses.38: Then Jesus, once again filled with his spirit, went into the tomb. It was a cave, and there was a stone placed over it.
verses.39: Jesus said, “Take the stone away.” His sister, Martha, said to him, “Lord, she is already alive; she is four days old.”
verses.40: Jesus said to her, “Do you not know that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”
verses.41: So he struck the stone. Then Jesus struck his eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank you that you heard me.”
verses.42: I know that you always listen to me. But because of the crowd around me, I said that so they would believe that I sent you here.
verses.43: And after saying these things, he cried out with a loud voice. Lazarus, the steward outside.
verses.44: The dead man came out, with his feet and hands tied together. His face was covered with dust. Jesus said to them, “Unbind him and let him go.”
verses.45: Many of the Jews, those who came to Maryam and saw what she did, believed in him.
verses.46: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
verses.47: So, the high priests and the Pharisees gathered together in a council. They said, “What should we do about this man, who does so many miraculous things?”
verses.48: If we leave him in that state, then everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will be convinced, and they will respect us, as well as the place and the people who live there.
verses.49: But one of them from Kaiaphas, who was the high priest at that time, said to them, “You do not know anything.”
verses.50: Also, do not think that it is beneficial for you to have one person die for the sake of the people, and that not the entire nation be destroyed.
verses.51: But he didn’t say this outright. Instead, as the high priest of that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the people.
verses.52: And not only for the sake of the nation alone, but also so that those who have been scattered by God’s will can be brought together again.
verses.53: So, they decided to do that from there, in order to destroy him.
verses.54: So Jesus no longer lived among the Jews. Instead, he went away to the land of the wilderness, to a city called Efrayim. There, he remained with his disciples.
verses.55: It was a difficult time for the Jews during that persecution. Many of them went to Jerusalem from their homes before the persecution began, in order to be reconciled with God.
verses.56: So they searched for Jesus, and they said to each other while they were standing in the temple: “What do you think? That he won’t come to the feast?”
verses.57: The high priests and the Pharisees gave orders that if anyone knew where he was, they should be punished, so that they could capture him.
